key_insight: Serum brain-derived tau (BD-tau) distinguished traumatic brain injury (TBI) from spinal cord injury (SCI) with high accuracy in acute neurotrauma cohorts.
clinical_relevance: BD-tau could support injury-specific triage and trial enrollment, but its role in routine care requires further validation.
method: Assessed baseline serum BD-tau in 285 patients with TBI, 57 with SCI, and 22 controls.
Compared discrimination with paired cerebrospinal fluid samples and established blood biomarkers.
Tracked serum BD-tau trajectories for up to 144 hours after injury.
evidence_signal: Overall TBI-versus-SCI discrimination reached AUC 0.91 (95% CI 0.87–0.96); separate analyses favored serum over cerebrospinal fluid BD-tau and established blood biomarkers.
watch_item: Performance in these neuro-intensive care cohorts may not generalize to broader emergency populations or mixed TBI–SCI injuries.
paper_title: Serum brain-derived tau distinguishes acute neurotrauma diagnoses
